questions.stem: What type of organic compounds are fats and oils?

options.text: Esters formed from glycerol and fatty acids

questions.explanation: Fats and oils are esters made from glycerol (an alcohol with three -OH groups) and long-chain carboxylic acids called fatty acids.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a fat and an oil?

options.text: Fats are solid at room temperature; oils are liquid
Oils contain carbon; fats do not
Fats dissolve in water; oils do not

questions.explanation: Fats are solid at room temperature (they contain more saturated fatty acids), while oils are liquid at room temperature (they contain more unsaturated fatty acids with C=C double bonds).

options.text: The hydrolysis of fats or oils with an alkali to make soap and glycerol

questions.explanation: Saponification is the process of making soap by hydrolysing fats or oils with a strong alkali (like sodium hydroxide). The products are soap (sodium salts of fatty acids) and glycerol.

questions.stem: Unsaturated fats contain C=C double bonds. How can they be converted to saturated fats?

options.text: By hydrogenation -- adding hydrogen across the double bonds using a nickel catalyst

questions.explanation: Hydrogenation adds hydrogen across the C=C double bonds in unsaturated oils, converting them to saturated fats. This is used to make margarine from vegetable oils.

questions.stem: How can you test whether a fat or oil is unsaturated?

options.text: Add bromine water; it will decolourise if C=C double bonds are present
Heat it and measure the boiling point

questions.explanation: Bromine water decolourises in the presence of C=C double bonds. If the oil is unsaturated, the bromine water will change from orange to colourless.

questions.stem: What are the two parts of a soap molecule?

options.text: A hydrophilic (water-loving) head and a hydrophobic (water-hating) tail
A metal part and a non-metal part
An acid part and a base part

questions.explanation: Soap molecules have a hydrophilic (ionic) head that dissolves in water and a hydrophobic (long hydrocarbon) tail that dissolves in grease. This allows soap to remove grease from surfaces.

questions.stem: Why is it healthier to consume unsaturated fats rather than saturated fats?

options.text: Saturated fats are linked to higher levels of cholesterol and heart disease

questions.explanation: Saturated fats are associated with increased blood cholesterol levels and a higher risk of heart disease. Unsaturated fats (found in fish, nuts, and vegetable oils) are considered healthier.
